subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Shah <sshar@acmehealth.com>, Laura Gomez <lgomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Hi Samir / Laura —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of our discussion and the proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Pain points we heard
- Peak inference latency spikes during batch processing windows (p95 frequently > 1.2s) impacting downstream workflows.
- Need for isolation (PHI concerns) — single-tenant environment preferred.
- Predictable throughput for nightly ML jobs and daytime interactive queries; burst capacity required for campaigns.

Goals / success criteria
- Dedicated GPU pool with customer isolation (VPC + private deployment options).
- P95 latency <= 300ms for online requests, background batch windows processed within nightly SLA window.
- 99.95% platform uptime SLA for the dedicated fleet.
- Clear security evidence for HIPAA controls and audit logs.

Initial sizing & configuration we discussed
- Baseline: 4x A100 GPUs reserved (preferred) with ability to burst to +2 GPUs for peak windows.
- Autoscale policy: scale up when queue > X and drop back after idle window; warm KV cache for top prefixes.
- Data plane: VPC peering + optional on-prem connector for audit log forwarding.

Attachments I shared
- acme-dedicated-capacity-sheet.xlsx (proposed sizing & cost estimate)
- redwood-dedicated-sla-draft.pdf (SLA draft and feature list)

Next steps
- You (Samir) to confirm whether you need 4 reserved GPUs or want to move to 8 as discussed in the call.
- I’ll loop in Solutions (Dylan) to validate the sizing and provide a perf test plan.
- Marissa will send procurement checklist and draft MSA/redlines we typically see for Private deployments.
- If confirmed, we can provision a short 7-day trial of a dedicated pool for validation before committing.

Proposed dates:
- Technical validation call with Dylan: Sep 28 (we’re flexible)
- Procurement target: PO by Oct 10 if sizing and SOW are aligned

If anything above is off or you want us to reword for your procurement team, tell me and I’ll update.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0123

Ben / Marissa —

Thanks for the detailed recap, that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- After internal review, we think baseline should be 6 reserved A100s rather than 4. Our busiest nightly job will need more headroom; we still want the ability to burst +2 on top of that.
- Latency target: p95 = 250ms for interactive endpoints (we can tolerate slightly higher for batch jobs).
- SLA: 99.9% is our procurement baseline; we can accept 99.95% if there’s clear credits and remediation timelines.

I attached the completed security questionnaire that the compliance team requested — the answers to the SOC2/HIPAA items are in there.

Procurement timeline: we’re aiming to finish procurement approvals and submit PO by Oct 8 (earlier if possible). If you can provide a short formal SOW and a draft PO invoice by next Tuesday (Sep 28), that would help speed things up.

Also, happy to have a technical validation session on Sep 29 at 10am PT with Dylan. Laura and I will both attend.

Samir
VP, Data Platform | Acme Health
